title: Validation Runtime and Error Behavior
readerIntent: Understand how validation executes, reports failures, and remains observable.
owner: Owning validation services, pipelines, status definitions, and response handlers
summary: Validation is executed through declarative schema rules, services, interceptors, and pipelines, then normalized into stable status codes and safe diagnostic context.

sections.heading: Runtime behavior
items: Collect normalized input and resolved request context.
Run the applicable validators in deterministic order.
Accumulate field-level errors where safe and useful; stop immediately for security or invariant failures that must not continue.
Reject through the owning pipeline error path.
Resolve a registered stable status code and transport response.
Attach safe trace and layer context for diagnostics.

sections.heading: Error contract
items: Stable machine code for clients and monitoring.
Appropriate response classification without exposing internals.
User-facing messages supplied through the presentation/content contract where applicable.
Structured field or context details only when authorized and non-sensitive.
No credentials, secrets, password hashes, unrestricted records, or raw provider errors.

sections.heading: Operational signals
items: Failure rate by safe validation code, capability, route, and runtime context.
Repeated invalid attempts and authorization denials.
Import rejection counts and reconciliation outcomes.
Validator latency and downstream work avoided.
Configuration preview and activation validation failures.

sections.heading: Field errors and invariant failures
paragraphs: Independent field problems can be accumulated so a user corrects several inputs at once. Security, tenant, ownership, and critical invariant failures stop processing immediately when continuing could reveal data or perform unsafe work.
The owning validator decides whether details are safe. A public response never includes raw database errors, internal stack traces, credentials, or inaccessible record content.

sections.heading: Stable status resolution
items: Every emitted success or error code is registered by its owner.
Response classification and HTTP mapping remain stable for clients.
Presentation text can be localized without changing the machine contract.
Trace context identifies the pipeline and layer for authorized diagnostics.
Unknown status codes fail validation rather than becoming accidental HTTP 500 behavior.

sections.heading: Transactions and side effects
paragraphs: Validation completes before irreversible side effects where possible. Multi-record changes use the supported transaction contract or explicit compensation. Events and external notifications follow the committed authoritative transition.
A transient provider error is not a validation failure. Runtime handling preserves this distinction so retry policy does not repeat deterministic invalid requests.

sections.heading: Example failure trace
paragraphs: An employee submits an Enterprise with a Tenant outside the authorized scope. Request shape is valid, but relationship policy rejects the target. The response uses a safe authorization or relationship status and does not confirm protected Tenant details.
Operators can correlate the request, capability, validation layer, safe tenant context, and outcome. Axis renders a friendly backend-driven message.

sections.heading: Performance and abuse protection
items: Run inexpensive deterministic checks before database or remote calls.
Bound collection sizes, nesting depth, query complexity, and error detail.
Monitor repeated invalid and unauthorized attempts without logging secrets.
Cache only validation data that remains permission-safe and correctly invalidated.
Load-test large imports and bulk validation independently from interactive requests.

sections.heading: Recovery and verification
items: Prove no state or derived event follows a rejected mutation.
Prove partial multi-record work rolls back or compensates.
Verify the same stable error through API, import, workflow, job, and assistant paths.
Verify localization does not alter machine codes.
Verify logs, metrics, and traces remain useful and non-sensitive.
Regression-test valid legacy records after rule changes.
